posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
I'm not sure what you're asking for. The point of a sample project is to look at how items and skills and enemies and classes are configured, so you can get some ideas.
Your project wouldn't use any of that. You're just making a story and tracking choices through variables or switches.
Basic tutorials on how to use the event system should cover that - what specific questions do you have? What don't you understand how to do?

posts.author: rpgLord69
posts.body:
Here's some tips:
-If you don't want to use a map, don't draw a map. Just use 'show picture' to show your BG picture. Actually it doesn't even matter if you draw a map because the picture goes on top of it, so you can even use the fence tiles to draw a picture of a **** and noone will see it.
-Show picture also works for the busts, but you can also google plugins for that.
-If your VN has choices, you'll probably want something to change how the 'show choices' looks. There's a plugin 'Galv's Visual Novel Choices MZ'. And like ATT_Turan said, the choices will just affect some switches and variables. Then you'll just use conditional branches to check the status of your switches/variables.
-If you want to do different routes that end in game end, you can use global switches/variables. VisuStella basic plugins let you do that.
-VisuStella basic plugins also let you show conditional options in your choices
-If you want to change the way your title scene works, there's VisuStella Event Title Scene (paid), but also you can look for free plugins.
-VisuStella also has (paid) visual novel plugins that add those kind of features commonly seen in many visual novels to the user interface.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
ryukia48 said:
and apply event systems, switches, or variables
Click to expand...
please follow the link to the starting point tutorial in my signature.
somewhat into that tutorial you'll find a link to the "Variables Guide", which is a game teaching how to use variables in general.
The rest of the tutorial might also help you, because a lot of it is general and maker-independent.
That said, there are different ways to handle VN inside a maker, and they all use the methods given by the maker to do so. So you will likely use maps (even f they are empty) to organise your VN-chapters as it would be difficult to manage all events for an entire story on a single map.
So even if you don't want to make a regular RPG, you should at least familarize yourself with the basics on how the makers work. Otherwise you'll have problems following any sample you might find.
